pr_body:
# Objective

Upgrade to Taffy 0.3.3

Fixes: #7712

## Solution

Upgrade to Taffy 0.3.3 with the `grid` feature disabled.

---

## Changelog
* Changed Taffy version to 0.3.3 and disabled its `grid` feature. 
* Added the `Start` and `End` variants to `AlignItems`, `AlignSelf`, `AlignContent` and `JustifyContent`.
* Added the `SpaceEvenly` variant to `AlignContent`.
* Updated `from_style` for Taffy 0.3.3.

I'm currently busy so I'll help tomorrow if needed(timezone: GMT+2)

We can add CSS grid support and remove `Val::Undefined` shortly after 0.10 drops.

issue_context.title: Pixel wide gaps between adjacent UI nodes
comments:
I think this is probably Taffy related. It seems to round the length of certain nodes but not others.

There are subtle problems with Bevy UI Text that are similar where what I suspect is happening is that you ask for a width of x pixels for your text with the MeasureFunc, but then Taffy rounds it down a pixel and so the Text no longer fits the width, so the last word of the text gets pushed down to a new line. But the Node itself stays at a height of only one line of text, so the text renderer doesn't draw the second line of text and it just looks there are missing words at the end of sentences with certain text layouts.

Hmm... I feel like the text renderer probably shouldn't count a glyph as fitting if it requires a partial pixel.

>  I think this is probably Taffy related. It seems to round the length of certain nodes but not others.

Taffy's rouding is pretty simple. It computes the entire layout using floats, and then rounds everything at the end.

I haven't really looked at this deeply yet, so I might be completely off. The scale factor code is all over the place, it might be something there. I'll recreate some of my examples just in Taffy and compare what happens.

I can see why this is happening. Unrounded results for @A-Walrus's test:

```
TREE
└──  FLEX [x: 0    y: 0    width: 963.3333 height: 1000] (3v1)
    ├──  LEAF [x: 381.36664 y: 0    width: 100.3 height: 100.3] (1v1)
    └──  LEAF [x: 481.66663 y: 0    width: 100.3 height: 100.3] (2v1)
```

child_a's x position is going to get rounded down. child_b's x position is going to get rounded up. It's not immediately obvious to me what the correct solution is though. Especially as I suspect the ideal solution would take into account the `devicePixelRatio` and round based on the size of physical pixels rather than logical ones, and perhaps even do subpixel rendering.

This quote quite neatly sums up the problem:

>  We’re trying to meet a bunch of constraints that can’t all be satisfied at the same time (the proof is left as an exercise to the reader, though I may have actually written it out once in a Bugzilla comment):
> 1. 4 adjacent objects of width/height 25% (for example) starting at one edge of a container should end exactly at the other edge; there should never be an extra pixel in the container and they should never be wrapped due to being a pixel to wide
> 2. objects that are logically adjacent should always touch visually; there should never be a pixel gap or a pixel of overlap due to rounding error
> 3. objects given the same width should occupy the same number of pixels
> 4. object boundaries should always (visually) be aliased to a specific pixel boundary in the display (they should never be blurred)
> 
> The one [Mozilla] sacrifices is typically (3), except for borders where we sacrifice (1) by rounding the widths to pixel boundaries much earlier.

(https://johnresig.com/blog/sub-pixel-problems-in-css/)

I tried looking into what browsers do, but there seems to be no easy way to tell because they won't give you programatic access to the values used for rendering (`getBoundingClientRect` will give you the unrounded floats, and `offsetLeft`/`offsetWidth` will give you values Taffy is already computing with the 1 pixel gap even though there isn't actually a 1px gap in the final render).

Yes, I understand now I think. The size of the root node doesn't matter. If you add another node to the example that wraps the two nodes it will be rounded up to 201 pixels wide, with the extra pixel either between or to the side of the two nodes, depending on the alignment.

This is issue is now fixed in Taffy and can be fixed in Bevy by upgrading to the latest Taffy (`v0.3.3`). This will require https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/7485 to be merged either first, or as part of the upgrade. The approach in [this branch](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/commit/84ac898128bfabb65fe4c814fc7f2f9542e9a84e#diff-ea54819d071882d7cad0d6bca53085597dfbdad16d95080d4f052bed2b332506R33) of disabling the `grid` feature for the initial upgrade is probably a sensible one.

review_comments: "cross axis" is true for Flexbox. But Grid has no "main" or "cross" axis. It only has "block" (vertical with left-to-right writing mode) and "inline" (horizontal with left-to-right writing mode). For grid, the `align*` properties apply to the block axis and the `justify*` properties apply to the inline axis.
